maria.s: Heads-up — rolling a small RBAC change that restricts the `audit_writer` role. Going to deploy at 18:00 UTC. Some older publisher clients may see 403s until they are patched.
ajay: Any required schema changes or just permission gating?
lina-sre: RBAC only, but we should validate events at ingest so customers get clear errors rather than silent drops.
maria.s: Agree. Ops wants explicit rejections on schema mismatch (400) and 403 for auth. That means client libs need to surface the error code.
kevin: For schema, can we add a soft-add field first? We plan to require `actor_org` in the next major. For now we should accept missing `actor_org` but include a warning and a customer-facing validation message.
ajay: Sounds good. Proposed JSON Schema (canary):
```
{
  "type":"object",
  "required":["ts","event_type","actor_id"],
  "properties":{
    "ts":{"type":"string"},
    "event_type":{"type":"string"},
    "actor_id":{"type":"string"},
    "actor_org":{"type":"string"},
    "payload":{"type":"object"}
  }
}
```
maria.s: Perfect — warning header when `actor_org` missing: `X-Audit-Warning: actor_org_missing`. We'll surface this in client SDK logs and customer web UI.
ops-bot: Note — KMS key rotation window scheduled 02:00-03:00 UTC. Any in-flight envelope decrypts will fall back to previous key for 48h.
lina-sre: Important: when KMS rotates, we see a small CPU bump on decrypt workers. Need to validate batch sizes to avoid backpressure.
kevin: Current defaults: batching = 250 events, flush_interval = 100ms. We've seen ingest spikes to ~60k eps leading to indexing lag. Two mitigation ideas: 1) adaptive batching (reduce to 100 when latency > 200ms); 2) shed non-customer-critical telemetry to S3 cold path.
ajay: Can we quantify index cost? Last calc: indexing into ES (hot nodes) ~ $0.015 per 1k events for our mapping (small payload). If we switch some fields to tokenized vs keyword it changes storage costs a lot.
maria.s: Also consider prefix/KV cache for repeated actor lookups to avoid repeated decryption calls to KMS. That should cut KMS ops by ~40% in our bench.
kevin: For customer-facing validation, we should return a structured error that includes `invalid_fields` and `example_fix`. Example response: `{ "code":"schema_error","invalid_fields":["actor_org"],"example_fix":"add \"actor_org\": \"acme\"" }`
lina-sre: During the last simulated surge, backpressure manifested as higher queue latency + 503s from the sink. If we add adaptive batching, we must also throttle producers earlier (429) to preserve SLO.
ajay: Proposal: rollout plan
- canary (10% ingesters) — validate warnings only, no hard reject. 
- metric run for 24h to measure KMS QPS, ES indexing lag, cost delta.
- stage (50%) — enable `X-Audit-Warning` surfaced in UI + client lib update.
- prod — require `actor_org`, RBAC change goes live, 403 behavior enforced.
kevin: I'll own the canary + perf dashboards. Need a script to inject missing `actor_org` events at 5% to measure false-positive hit rate.
maria.s: Ajay will update SDKs to interpret `X-Audit-Warning` and surface user-friendly messages. Lina will run KMS perf tests and tune batch sizes. Kevin will monitor indexing cost. Ops will block deploy if the 99p latency increases > 25%.
ops-bot: Action created — #runbook: audit-schema-rollout (assigned: ajay, kevin, lina, maria.s).
ajay: Quick Q on vulnerability triage — if we see a malformed event that triggers a panic in decoder, do we map that to incident or just schema error?
lina-sre: Anything that causes process crash -> incident (P1). Otherwise a schema error -> normal alerting + customer validation queue.
maria.s: Noted. Also add an acceptance test that ensures malformed events produce a non-fatal rejection path.
kevin: I'll schedule a 2-hour canary window tomorrow. Posting time shortly. :thumbsup:
